mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following a UNRATE decrease, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates expanding residential construction, which may boost related industries and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase but the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the subsequent 60-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% may signal tighter monetary policy, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, and thus negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 20-day periods following a FEDFUNDS increase above 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) reflects higher economic activity, which may lead to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases but the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the subsequent 60-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) may indicate deflationary pressures, leading to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by more than 0.5% in a month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 35% of the 20-day periods following a CPIAUCSL decrease, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 45% of the 20-day periods following a PAYEMS increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which may stimulate borrowing and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day periods following a FEDFUNDS decrease, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real disposable income (RSAFS) indicates higher consumer purchasing power, which may boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If real disposable income increases but the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the subsequent 20-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.
